title: Release validation orchestrator: regression fingerprinting & golden-run comparisons
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Problem: As we introduce more model variants and kernel optimizations, small regressions in token-level latency or subtle behavioral drift can slip past unit tests and break production quality SLAs during rollouts. Existing validation is a mix of ad-hoc smoke tests and manual golden comparisons; we need a deterministic, automated orchestration that runs a battery of checks before allowing a rollout stage to progress.

Goal: Implement an orchestrator (validation-run controller) that composes smoke tests, performance regressions gates, and behavioral eval suites into a single pre-deploy validation pass. The orchestrator should produce a compact fingerprint for the candidate release and compare it against a golden-run baseline to detect regressions that matter to customers (latency, tail-latency, token-cost, hallucination rate on anchor prompts). It must integrate with the rollout system to signal pass/fail and to emit structured diagnostics for on-call and product owners.

Scope: Core work covers the orchestration logic, baseline/golden-run storage and diffing, perf gate thresholds, and integration with the canary rollout API. Out of scope for this ticket: UI/Console surfaces for the validation results (separate PM/Console work), and long-term retention of full traces (we will store summarized fingerprints and links to traces).
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible validation-run API accepts a release candidate tag and produces a JSON fingerprint that includes latency P50/P95/P99, token-cost delta, eval-suite pass rates, and KV-cache-warmup profile.
Automated comparison tool flags regressions when any configured threshold is exceeded and returns a human-readable summary with top-3 contributing tests/metrics.
The orchestrator can be invoked by the rollout pipeline and will return a deterministic pass/fail result within the configured SLO (default 30 minutes).
Integrations: sends structured result to rollout-controller (internal API), writes fingerprint artifact to S3, and logs links to perf dashboards and failing eval runs.
End-to-end smoke: a synthetic canary flow runs against a nightly build and demonstrates an intentional perf regression is caught and blocks the rollout.
plan: Design validation-run manifest schema (inputs, test selectors, thresholds, runtime knobs).
Implement runner for smoke tests and perf probes (parallelizable, re-usable across environments).
Build fingerprint comparator service that computes diffs and ranks contributing regressions by impact score.
Wire orchestrator into rollout-controller with a synchronous validate() endpoint and async artifact publishing.
Create a minimal on-call playbook and alert rules for validation failures (link in links).
Run 3 pilot validations against runtime-1.22 candidate images, iterate thresholds based on observed noise.
decisions: Use synthetic anchor prompts plus production-sampled traces for behavioral evals to balance determinism and real-world coverage.
Fingerprints will store aggregated buckets (P50/P75/P90/P95/P99) instead of full traces to limit storage and speed comparisons.
Comparison uses impact scoring: combine absolute delta and request-weighted frequency to surface regressions that matter for cost/latency.
Default perf gate: block if P99 latency increases by >15% or token-cost increases by >8% compared to golden-run; thresholds tuned during pilot.
risks_and_mitigation: False positives from noisy benchmarks: mitigate by running 3 independent runs and using median fingerprint; build noise model for known flakey tests.
Blocking too many rollouts: provide 'soft-fail' mode for early weeks where failures are reported but not blocked; require explicit opt-in to hard block for critical customers.
Golden-run drift: periodically rebaseline golden runs after validated major changes; require owner approval for baseline updates.
Runtime cost of running full evals: support tiered execution where quick smoke + targeted perf probes run by default and full eval-suite is gated to weekly/nightly.

2026-02-18 Mei Wong: Spike results: KV-cache warmup adds variance—we should include warmup window profiling in the fingerprint. Added to plan. (see PR 4321)
2026-02-23 Priya Rao (SRE): Reviewed thresholds. Recommended using relative and absolute thresholds for tail-latency to avoid blocking on microsecond variances. Updated decisions accordingly.

2026-02-27 Design review (Sofia Martinez): Requested clear UX hooks for console (pass/fail reason and top contributing tests). Not implementing UI in this ticket but added link in plan for follow-up PM work.

2026-03-01 Mei Wong: Implemented runner for smoke tests and perf probes. Pushed initial comparator scaffold to branch 'validation-orch/comp-sca'. Need help tuning noise model; flagged ENG-17655 to own noise-model work.
